text.p: Nasdaq stocks closed lower on Friday with leading technology stocks dropping on profit taking.
The Nasdaq Composite Index was down 13.41 points, or 1.03 percent, at 1284.92. Decliners led advancers by 2474 to 1733 on volume of about 568 million shares.
"Technology stocks, they never really got going," said Frank Calta, director of trading at Anvil Institutional Services.
Major technology stocks such as Microsoft Corp and Intel Corp "have been straight up like a rocket and they look tired," he said.
Microsoft was off one to 80 and Intel fell 4-1/2 to 132-3/8. Oracle Corp fell 3-1/4 to 44 on heavy volume of 25.2 million shares after the software publisher reported weak European sales.
Among stocks bucking the downtrend was Interlink Computer Sciences Inc which closed up 3-15/16, or more than 33 percent, to 15-5/8 on news it and Cisco Systems Inc had formed a strategic alliance.
